content.text:
name: Bench

# Runs the fa coding agent against terminal-bench on Linux runners
# (issue #125). The `dart build cli` bundle must be a Linux x64 binary to
# match the task container's arch — a macOS host bundle fails with
# "cannot execute binary file", so this cannot run locally on macOS.
#
# Sharded matrix (issue #132): the full terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 dataset
# is 80 tasks at ~11 min each — ~14 h sequential, past even the 6 h job
# cap. Shape: setup (build bundle, resolve task ids into shards) → one
# matrix job per shard → merge job aggregating overall accuracy. Small
# `tasks` inputs degenerate to a single-shard matrix, so the hello-world
# smoke path is unchanged.
#
# Issue #142 (baseline run 34576017658, 26/80 = 32.5%): shards are balanced
# by declared task budget (LPT) instead of contiguous split, tb runs with
# --global-timeout-multiplier 2 (the dataset's declared timeouts — median
# 360s agent / 60s test — assume fast models and warm container networks;
# the baseline lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
# phases still apt-installing their own deps when the cap hit), and the
# bench job patches the downloaded dataset so debian:-based task images
# build again after Debian archived bullseye (expired Release file kills
# `apt-get update` during docker compose build).
#
# Issue #1122: the flat agent cap becomes a per-run ladder — `agent-timeout`
# (base cap seconds) plus optional `progress-extension` (deadline recedes
# while the agent's rendered output grows; idle window 120s, hard ceiling
# 4x base, decisions audited per trial). With both inputs absent the run
# is byte-for-byte today's behavior (dataset declared caps x multiplier;
# REG-1). E3 shard math: with extension on, worst case per task is the
# ceiling (4x agent-timeout) + test budget — the defaults fit the current
# LPT sizing below; raise the ceiling and shrink shards accordingly.
#
# Issue gh-1206 (run 37144207185): the DECLARED test budgets (tb default
# 60s = 120s effective at multiplier 2) classify slow-but-healthy verifier
# phases as test_timeout — jupyter-notebook-server died with the agent's
# pane DONE, the tests having burned their own budget on first-boot
# server startup + in-container dep installs. The test-side analog of the
# #1122 knobs: `test-timeout-floor` (default 120s declared = 240s
# effective) pads every task's max_test_timeout_sec up to the floor in
# the downloaded dataset (patch_test_timeouts.py — the same in-place
# patch mechanism as the Debian apt fix), and shard_tasks.py sizes shards
# on the padded budgets so LPT never under-counts. The cap is a cap, not
# a wait: fast verifier phases are unaffected (a full-dataset worst case
# grows < 10 min/shard); `0` restores the declared budgets.
#
# Issue gh-1407 (runs 37609468473 + 37736364517): the floor alone left
# repeat-offender tasks (jupyter-notebook-server, build-initramfs-qemu)
# test_timeout at the cap in every round — the budget measured runner
# luck, not agent capability. patch_test_timeouts.py additionally applies
# the per-task override table (test_budget_overrides.json, checked in
# next to it: runner-measured test-phase p95 per task, effective budget
# = max(declared, p95 x 1.5) — a slow-suite fix, NOT a global floor
# bump), and shard_tasks.py emits a ::warning:: fairness annotation when
# a planned task's effective test budget is still below its measured
# p95 (fairness_warnings job output), so a structurally-unpassable
# configuration is caught at planning time.
#
# Issue #1392 (bench round 3): retire the artificial timeout class. The
# ×4 ladder ceiling itself was the round-2 killer (play-zork died at 72
# productive minutes), so with progress-extension ON the ladder ceiling
# becomes an absolute one (3600s default, FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC)
# and the outer harness cap pins above THAT — a trial only dies by the
# adapter's verdict (stall / abs ceiling), never tb's flat wait_for. The
# experiment: split 8 shards, run at most `max-concurrent` (default 2) —
# GHA's strategy.max-parallel IS the semaphore. Shards are LPT-packed to
# the job cap minus 15 min headroom; the merge report degrades cancelled
# shards to a `coverage: X/N` note (never red from aggregation), carries
# per-request latency p50/p95 per concurrency level from each trial's
# bench_metrics.json, and names any agent_timeout trial whose session
# gaps never reached the 240s stall threshold (the round-2 contradiction,
# AC8).
# gh-1471 (run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks when the z.ai quota died
# mid-run): the provider stops being a hardcode — every dispatch picks
# zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to today) or kimi-for-coding
# k3-256k via a dedicated FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY (never the review factory's
# KIMI_REVIEW_KEY — one quota must not serve both), or `custom`: a
# provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step (https-only baseUrl,
# no key-like fields — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata) whose
# key comes only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM. A
# setup-job resolve step maps the choice to the full provider triple and
# preflights the selected secret BEFORE any shard starts (presence only,
# never a value); the shard job names the provider+model (job `name:`
# CAN read needs outputs — unlike env), and the summary report tags it
# (BENCH_RUN_LABEL) so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/cost
# views.
run-name: fa bench · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container
              # boot after shards start. `type` is allowed here (it rides
              # the FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output) but stripped from the
              # emitted config below.
              unsupported=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                [. | keys[]
                  | select(. as $k
                      | ["baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens","input","thinkingLevel","type"]
                      | index($k) | not)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$unsupported" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config has unsupported key(s): $unsupported — supported keys: baseUrl, model, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel (type selects FA_PROVIDER_TYPE and is not echoed into FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `type` feeds the container's catalog lookup via
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: when declared it must be a non-empty
              # string (jq's `//` treats "" as present, so an explicit
              # check is required); undeclared/null defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("type") and .type != null then (.type | type == "string" and test("\\S")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"type\" must be a non-empty string naming a catalog provider (e.g. \"openai\") when declared"; exit 1
              fi
              # The capability pair mirrors _parseCapabilityInt: JSON
              # integers at or above the Dart resolver floors
              # (minOverrideContextWindow 16384 / minOverrideMaxTokens
              # 1024 — the same boundaries as the yaml overrides layer);
              # blank string / null are ABSENT, like every other optional
              # input; anything else throws at container boot today.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '
                def capok(min): . as $v
                  | $v == null or (($v | type) == "string" and ($v | test("^\\s*$")))
                  or (($v | type) == "number" and ($v | floor) == $v and $v >= min);
                (.contextWindow | capok(16384)) and (.maxTokens | capok(1024))
              ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config contextWindow/maxTokens must be integers at or above the Dart resolver floors (contextWindow >= 16384, maxTokens >= 1024) — a below-floor or non-integer declaration would fail loud at every trial's container boot"; exit 1
              fi
              # `input` mirrors _parseInputList: a non-empty list whose
              # entries are exactly "text"/"image".
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("input") then (.input | type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; . == "text" or . == "image")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"input\" must be a non-empty list of \"text\"/\"image\" entries (the Dart preconfig's contract)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `thinkingLevel` mirrors _parseThinkingLevel: a blank
              # string is absent; otherwise one of the
              # configThinkingLevels ladder (xhigh/max fold to high
              # Dart-side).
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("thinkingLevel") then (.thinkingLevel | if type == "string" then (test("^\\s*$") or (. as $l | ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] | index($l) != null)) else false end) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"thinkingLevel\" must be one of minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the Dart preconfig's ladder)"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Passthrough: every declared field rides the config
              # verbatim EXCEPT "type" — it already rides the dedicated
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output/env, and the Dart preconfig's
              # FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG whitelist has no "type" key (it would
              # throw at every trial's container boot). Blank/null
              # capability fields are dropped (Dart-side they are
              # ABSENT, like every other optional input — the emitted
              # config declares only what is effective). Plus the fixed
              # key-env injection; `type` defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '
                del(.type)
                | del(.contextWindow | select(. == null or ((. | type) == "string" and (. | test("^\\s*$")))))
                | del(.maxTokens | select(. == null or ((. | type) == "string" and (. | test("^\\s*$")))))
                | . + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # fa-setup.sh.j2 extracts bin/fah at the top level.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux x64)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench's CLI breaks on Python 3.14 (typer: 'function' object
      # is not subscriptable).
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      - run: pip install terminal-bench

      # stdlib-only unit tests for the bench scripts; a shard/patch bug
      # costs a multi-hour run, so gate shard resolution on them.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v

      # gh-1206: the shards must be sized on the SAME padded test budgets
      # the bench job writes into its dataset cache — an under-count here
      # could push a shard past the 355-min job cap.
      # Resolve the task-id list exactly like tb does (union of Path.glob
      # matches per -t pattern, against a dataset fetched via tb itself),
      # then balance shards longest-declared-budget-first (LPT, issue #142)
      # so no shard's worst case exceeds the job timeout; empty shards are
      # dropped, so a single-id smoke input degenerates to a one-job matrix.
      - name: Resolve task ids into shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR: ${{ inputs.test-timeout-floor }}
        run: |
          tb datasets download -d "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          python bench/terminal_bench/shard_tasks.py \
            --dataset-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --shards "$SHARDS" --tasks "$TASKS" \
            --test-timeout-floor "$TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR" \
            --job-cap-seconds "$((355 * 60))"
          # --job-cap-seconds takes the RAW job cap (355 min): the packer
          # subtracts its own 15-min headroom (shard_tasks.HEADROOM_SEC),
          # so the packed worst case lands at 340 min usable. Round 2 lost
          # shard-0 by ~1 min with zero headroom.

  bench:
    # gh-1471: the display name cannot read ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }} — the
    # env context is not available in job names (run 37580748776 died at
    # workflow startup on that) — but needs outputs ARE (same pattern as
    # bench-harbor.yml), so every shard names the provider+model: glm and
    # kimi runs never blend in the run history.
    name: fa on terminal-bench · ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }}
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Worst case per shard is LPT-packed to 340 min (job cap − 15 min
    # headroom, issue #1392); 355 min covers it under the 6 h runner cap.
    # --n-concurrent 1 keeps the math sequential-predictable and the total
    # concurrent LLM load at max-parallel x 1 (z.ai rate limits).
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # Issue #1392 ShardStagger: split 8, run at most `max-concurrent`
      # (default 2) at once — GHA queues the rest and starts each the
      # moment a slot frees. This IS the concurrency experiment's
      # semaphore; no runner-side coordination.
      max-parallel: ${{ fromJSON(inputs.max-concurrent) }}
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      - run: pip install terminal-bench

      # Populate tb's dataset cache, then patch it in place (tb run reuses a
      # non-empty cache without overwriting): debian:-based task images
      # cannot `apt-get update` during docker compose build since Debian
      # archived bullseye (issue #142).
      - name: Download & patch dataset
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR: ${{ inputs.test-timeout-floor }}
        run: |
          tb datasets download -d "$DATASET"
          python bench/terminal_bench/patch_dataset.py \
            "$HOME/.cache/terminal-bench/${DATASET%%==*}/${DATASET##*==}"
          # gh-1206: pad declared test budgets up to the floor so
          # slow-start verifier phases (jupyter, databases; judge phases
          # apt/pip-installing their own deps) stop dying as test_timeout
          # while the agent's work is already done. Empty/0 input = no
          # floor (declared budgets byte-for-byte).
          python bench/terminal_bench/patch_test_timeouts.py \
            "$HOME/.cache/terminal-bench/${DATASET%%==*}/${DATASET##*==}" \
            --floor "$TEST_TIMEOUT_FLOOR"

      - name: Run terminal-bench (fa agent)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/terminal_bench
          # gh-1471: the provider triple is resolved once in the setup
          # job (preflighted secret + hard fail on an unmapped choice) —
          # the shard only consumes it. All three bench keys are mapped
          # here (custom's AC 2a: key only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY); the
          # run block picks the resolved one by name, fa_agent.py ships
          # exactly that key into the container.
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_type }}
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_config }}
          FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_key_env }}
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # dataset task dir names: no whitespace, safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
          # Issue #1392: the forensics layer is opt-in by env — this run IS
          # the instrumented experiment, so it opts in deliberately (the
          # adapter forwards these into the container base64-encoded via
          # _CONN_ENV_KEYS). ConnTrace gives every trial's bench_metrics.json
          # its per-request/watchdog events and the [fa-bench] live lines;
          # the payload snapshot is what StallSentinel's hang-*.json
          # captures (see FA_CONN_PAYLOAD_KEEP_AUTH — the snapshot redacts
          # auth unless that is set, which bench never does).
          FA_CONN_DEBUG: '1'
          FA_CONN_TRACE_FILE: /tmp/fa-conn-trace.jsonl
          FA_CONN_PAYLOAD_SNAPSHOT: /tmp/fa-conn-snapshot.json
          # The concurrency level lands in every trial's bench_metrics.json
          # (concurrency_level) and the report's per-level latency block.
          FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY: ${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1471 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-t "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs: absent inputs leave both env vars unset — the
          # adapter then delegates to the stock flat-cap behavior (REG-1).
          # gh-1209: while a ladder is active, the outer harness cap MUST sit
          # above the ladder ceiling. On its own flat wait_for timeout tb
          # fabricates a zero-token AGENT_TIMEOUT result and discards the
          # adapter's usage-folded one — only a ladder-decided kill returns
          # the real token/cost numbers into results.json.
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) PROGRESS_EXTENSION_ON=1;;
            *) PROGRESS_EXTENSION_ON=;;
          esac
          ladder_base=''
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            # gh-1209 review: 0 passes the digit check but
            # TimeoutKnobs.from_env → _number then raises ValueError inside
            # EVERY trial's perform_task — reject it here so a bad input
            # costs one step, not a whole multi-hour shard.
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in
              0) echo '::error::agent-timeout must be a positive integer number of seconds'; exit 1;;
              *[!0-9]*) echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;;
            esac
            # Force base-10: $((...)) reads leading zeros as octal, so an
            # input like '010' would silently mean 8.
            ladder_base=$((10#$AGENT_TIMEOUT))
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
          elif [ -n "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION_ON" ]; then
            # Extension on with no explicit base runs the ladder at its
            # 360s default (fa_agent_timeout._BASE_DEFAULT) — pin the base
            # explicitly so the cap below and the ladder agree on one number.
            ladder_base=360
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$ladder_base"
          fi
          if [ -n "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION_ON" ]; then
            export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # Round-3 review: extension on ALONE leaves the legacy x4
            # ladder deciding (TimeoutKnobs.watch_active keys on a watch
            # knob). Export the abs ceiling — default 3600s — so the
            # progress watch, not the ladder, decides every kill.
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-3600}"
            # Issue #1392: with the progress watch on, the ladder's
            # ceiling is the ABS ceiling (default 3600s) — the old 4x+180
            # pin would guillotine an extended-but-progressing trial
            # below our own decision point. Pin the harness cap above the
            # abs ceiling so the adapter's verdict, not tb's flat
            # wait_for, decides every kill.
            args+=(--global-agent-timeout-sec \
              "$(( ${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-3600} + 180 ))")
          elif [ -n "$ladder_base" ]; then
            # Flat ladder only: outer harness cap above the ladder ceiling
            # (4x base + slack) so the ladder decides, never the flat
            # harness wait_for.
            args+=(--global-agent-timeout-sec "$((ladder_base * 4 + 180))")
          fi
          # Pinned --run-id: one tb-runs/shard-N/ dir per shard, so the merge
          # job's downloads cannot collide on tb's timestamped default.
          tb run -d "$DATASET" --agent-import-path fa_agent:FaAgent \
            --output-path tb-runs --no-cleanup --n-concurrent 1 \
            --global-timeout-multiplier 2 \
            --run-id "shard-${{ matrix.i }}" "${args[@]}"

      - name: Upload tb runs (shard ${{ matrix.i }})
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: tb-runs-shard-${{ matrix.i }}
          path: tb-runs/

      # Informational per-shard tally (--no-fail); the verdict is the merge
      # job's, over all shards.
      - name: Shard accuracy summary
        if: always()
        env:
          # Issue #1339 AC3: cost needs the model id, and a trial's id only
          # surfaces from its fa session logs — when those never reach the
          # artifact every row prices n/a. Pinned to the run's own model.
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1471: the report names the provider+model — glm and kimi
          # runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
        run: |
          python bench/terminal_bench/summary.py --no-fail tb-runs

  merge:
    name: Aggregate accuracy
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: tb-runs-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: tb-runs

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Issue #1392 AC4/AC7: re-own attribution after the fact — rows that
      # recorded 0/0 (tb's flat-cap fabrication discards the adapter's
      # fold) get their totals summed from the exported fa session JSONL,
      # ExportGuard gaps and AC8 score-honesty violations print loudly.
      # Runs BEFORE the merged upload so tb-runs-merged is the patched,
      # analysis-ready record — the durable artifact must not carry the
      # 0/0 rows this pass exists to fix.
      - name: Post-mortem attribution pass
        if: always()
        run: |
          python bench/post_mortem_usage.py tb-runs || true

      # tb exits 0 even with unresolved tasks; the verdict here (via
      # summary.py) covers run completeness — every expected task attempted
      # — after the merged artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged tb runs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: tb-runs-merged
          path: tb-runs/

      - name: Accuracy summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          # Issue #1339 AC3: same pin as the shard summary — price every
          # trial even when its fa session logs are absent.
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1471: same provider tag as the shard summary.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          # Issue #1392: the report tags the run's concurrency level —
          # the 8-shard/at-most-2 experiment is only comparable when the
          # level it ran at is on the record.
          BENCH_CONCURRENCY: ${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}
        run: |
          python bench/terminal_bench/summary.py tb-runs "$EXPECTED"

name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Resolve the dispatch input (family label, bare version, or full
      # Harbor id) to the canonical dataset id; unknown or version-less
      # specs fail fast here, before any download.
      - name: Resolve Terminal-Bench family
        id: family
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
        run: python bench/harbor_fa/families.py resolve "$DATASET"

      # Cost guard (issue #1124 E3): full runs of the intermediate
      # families are hours of GPU + LLM spend — require explicit
      # confirmation. Smoke runs (non-empty tasks) and 4.0 (the
      # historical default, AC4) are unaffected.
      - name: Confirm full intermediate-family run
        if: steps.family.outputs.family != '4.0' && inputs.confirm-full-run != true
        env:
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
        run: |
          # split_tasks.py strips each comma-glob before use, so " ", ",",
          # " , " all normalize to zero globs = a FULL dataset run. Judge
          # emptiness on that same normalization, not the raw input.
          if [ -z "$(printf %s "$TASKS" | tr -d '[:space:],')" ]; then
            echo "::error::Full run of Terminal-Bench ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }} (${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}, ~${{ steps.family.outputs.tasks }} tasks x $ATTEMPTS attempts) requires confirm-full-run: true. Smoke first: tasks=${{ steps.family.outputs.smoke }}, attempts=1 (docs/bench.md)."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) and bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py
      # plumbing the bench dirs don't have.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"
          [ -d "$ds_dir" ] || ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.
          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

  bench:
    name: fa on tbench ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ inputs.model }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench agent caps
    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    env:
      FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
      DATASET: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      # The optional self-hosted runner is a macOS box: setup-python cannot
      # write the hosted tool cache there (mkdir /Users/runner denied) and the
      # runner's own python3 is 3.14 — typer-based CLIs (harbor) break on 3.14.
      # The uv-managed CPython 3.13 user-space install below works on BOTH
      # runner kinds (the ubuntu-latest default included); uv is also the
      # canonical harbor install per the 4.0 docs.
      - name: Install harbor (uv-managed python 3.13)
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          uv venv --python 3.13 .bench-venv
          uv pip install --python .bench-venv/bin/python 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
          .bench-venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print("venv python:", sys.version.split()[0])'

      - name: Run harbor (fa agent, ${{ matrix.env }} env)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/harbor_fa
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}'
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_ID: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_ID }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET }}
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ inputs.model }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          NCONC: ${{ inputs.n-concurrent }}
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [ -n "$FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI" ] || { echo '::error::FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY secret is not set'; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py); absent inputs stay byte-for-byte
          # today's run (REG-1). A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # Pinned --job-name: one jobs/<name>/ dir per shard, so the summary
          # job's downloads cannot collide on harbor's timestamped default.
          # The family label keys results per dataset version (fa-4.0-*
          # matches the historical 4.0 names exactly).
          .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
            -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
            --job-name "fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${{ matrix.kind }}-${{ matrix.i }}" -o jobs \
            "${args[@]}"

      - name: Upload harbor job (shard ${{ matrix.i }})
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: harbor-job-shard-${{ matrix.i }}
          path: jobs/

      - name: Upload to Harbor Hub
        if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''
        env:
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          for job_dir in jobs/fa-${FAMILY}-*; do
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor upload "$job_dir" --public
          done

  summary:
    name: Aggregate resolution rate
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: harbor-job-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: jobs

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          MODEL: ${{ inputs.model }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" jobs

blocks.text:
# gh-1503: [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only

## Description

## Problem

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

Port the #1471 design onto `bench-harbor.yml`, reusing the exact same mapping (single source — extract the resolve step into a composite action or shared script if that kills the duplication; otherwise a byte-consistent copy with a cross-reference comment in both files):

1. `provider` choice input (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`) + `provider-config` for custom — same semantics, same validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-looking fields, jq-parse hard-fail).
2. kimi maps to type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384, key env from `secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`.
3. Preflight: selected provider's secret missing → fail in the first minute (today only the zai key is checked at :264).
4. Run identity: workflow/job names + summary carry provider+model (bench.yml pattern: `fa bench · <provider> · <model>`); the free-text `model` input becomes derived-from-provider (keep it as override only for `custom`, or drop it if redundant).
5. REG: default dispatch (no provider input) resolves byte-identical to today's zai glm wiring.
6. `n-concurrent` default is 1 ("z.ai rate-limit safe") — keep for zai; document the kimi-safe value in the input description (kimi coding plan tolerates more; owner picks at dispatch).

## Acceptance

- `bench-harbor.yml` dispatchable with `provider=kimi-for-coding`; smoke run (one task, e.g. the family smoke per docs/bench.md) green on TB 2.1 with kimi.
- actionlint + the workflow-shape tests extended for the new inputs/mapping (mirror of #1475's tests).
- Default-path REG green.

- #1471 (design), PR #1475 (bench.yml implementation to mirror)
- bench-harbor.yml:247-264 (current hardcode)
- kimi wiring precedent: ~/.fah/config.yaml custom providers (apiType kimi, k3-256k)

blocks.text:
name: Bench

# Runs the fa coding agent against terminal-bench on Linux runners
# (issue #125). The `dart build cli` bundle must be a Linux x64 binary to
# match the task container's arch — a macOS host bundle fails with
# "cannot execute binary file", so this cannot run locally on macOS.
#
# Sharded matrix (issue #132): the full terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 dataset
# is 80 tasks at ~11 min each — ~14 h sequential, past even the 6 h job
# cap. Shape: setup (build bundle, resolve task ids into shards) → one
# matrix job per shard → merge job aggregating overall accuracy. Small
# `tasks` inputs degenerate to a single-shard matrix, so the hello-world
# smoke path is unchanged.
#
# Issue #142 (baseline run 34576017658, 26/80 = 32.5%): shards are balanced
# by declared task budget (LPT) instead of contiguous split, tb runs with
# --global-timeout-multiplier 2 (the dataset's declared timeouts — median
# 360s agent / 60s test — assume fast models and warm container networks;
# the baseline lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
# phases still apt-installing their own deps when the cap hit), and the
# bench job patches the downloaded dataset so debian:-based task images
# build again after Debian archived bullseye (expired Release file kills
# `apt-get update` during docker compose build).
#
# Issue #1122: the flat agent cap becomes a per-run ladder — `agent-timeout`
# (base cap seconds) plus optional `progress-extension` (deadline recedes
# while the agent's rendered output grows; idle window 120s, hard ceiling
# 4x base, decisions audited per trial). With both inputs absent the run
# is byte-for-byte today's behavior (dataset declared caps x multiplier;
# REG-1). E3 shard math: with extension on, worst case per task is the
# ceiling (4x agent-timeout) + test budget — the defaults fit the current
# LPT sizing below; raise the ceiling and shrink shards accordingly.
#
# Issue gh-1206 (run 37144207185): the DECLARED test budgets (tb default
# 60s = 120s effective at multiplier 2) classify slow-but-healthy verifier
# phases as test_timeout — jupyter-notebook-server died with the agent's
# pane DONE, the tests having burned their own budget on first-boot
# server startup + in-container dep installs. The test-side analog of the
# #1122 knobs: `test-timeout-floor` (default 120s declared = 240s
# effective) pads every task's max_test_timeout_sec up to the floor in
# the downloaded dataset (patch_test_timeouts.py — the same in-place
# patch mechanism as the Debian apt fix), and shard_tasks.py sizes shards
# on the padded budgets so LPT never under-counts. The cap is a cap, not
# a wait: fast verifier phases are unaffected (a full-dataset worst case
# grows < 10 min/shard); `0` restores the declared budgets.
#
# Issue gh-1407 (runs 37609468473 + 37736364517): the floor alone left
# repeat-offender tasks (jupyter-notebook-server, build-initramfs-qemu)
# test_timeout at the cap in every round — the budget measured runner
# luck, not agent capability. patch_test_timeouts.py additionally applies
# the per-task override table (test_budget_overrides.json, checked in
# next to it: runner-measured test-phase p95 per task, effective budget
# = max(declared, p95 x 1.5) — a slow-suite fix, NOT a global floor
# bump), and shard_tasks.py emits a ::warning:: fairness annotation when
# a planned task's effective test budget is still below its measured
# p95 (fairness_warnings job output), so a structurally-unpassable
# configuration is caught at planning time.
#
# Issue #1392 (bench round 3): retire the artificial timeout class. The
# ×4 ladder ceiling itself was the round-2 killer (play-zork died at 72
# productive minutes), so with progress-extension ON the ladder ceiling
# becomes an absolute one (3600s default, FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC)
# and the outer harness cap pins above THAT — a trial only dies by the
# adapter's verdict (stall / abs ceiling), never tb's flat wait_for. The
# experiment: split 8 shards, run at most `max-concurrent` (default 2) —
# GHA's strategy.max-parallel IS the semaphore. Shards are LPT-packed to
# the job cap minus 15 min headroom; the merge report degrades cancelled
# shards to a `coverage: X/N` note (never red from aggregation), carries
# per-request latency p50/p95 per concurrency level from each trial's
# bench_metrics.json, and names any agent_timeout trial whose session
# gaps never reached the 240s stall threshold (the round-2 contradiction,
# AC8).
# gh-1471 (run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks when the z.ai quota died
# mid-run): the provider stops being a hardcode — every dispatch picks
# zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to today) or kimi-for-coding
# k3-256k via a dedicated FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY (never the review factory's
# KIMI_REVIEW_KEY — one quota must not serve both), or `custom`: a
# provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step (https-only baseUrl,
# no key-like fields — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata) whose
# key comes only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM. A
# setup-job resolve step maps the choice to the full provider triple and
# preflights the selected secret BEFORE any shard starts (presence only,
# never a value); the shard job names the provider+model (job `name:`
# CAN read needs outputs — unlike env), and the summary report tags it
# (BENCH_RUN_LABEL) so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/cost
# views.
run-name: fa bench · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider…

name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issu…

blocks.text:
name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Resolve the dispatch input (family label, bare version, or full
      # Harbor id) to the canonical dataset id; unknown or version-less
      # specs fail fast here, before any download.
      - name: Resolve Terminal-Bench family
        id: family
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
        run: python bench/harbor_fa/families.py resolve "$DATASET"

      # Cost guard (issue #1124 E3): full runs of the intermediate
      # families are hours of GPU + LLM spend — require explicit
      # confirmation. Smoke runs (non-empty tasks) and 4.0 (the
      # historical default, AC4) are unaffected.
      - name: Confirm full intermediate-family run
        if: steps.family.outputs.family != '4.0' && inputs.confirm-full-run != true
        env:
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
        run: |
          # split_tasks.py strips each comma-glob before use, so " ", ",",
          # " , " all normalize to zero globs = a FULL dataset run. Judge
          # emptiness on that same normalization, not the raw input.
          if [ -z "$(printf %s "$TASKS" | tr -d '[:space:],')" ]; then
            echo "::error::Full run of Terminal-Bench ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }} (${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}, ~${{ steps.family.outputs.tasks }} tasks x $ATTEMPTS attempts) requires confirm-full-run: true. Smoke first: tasks=${{ steps.family.outputs.smoke }}, attempts=1 (docs/bench.md)."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) and bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py
      # plumbing the bench dirs don't have.

blocks.text:
# gh-1503: [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only

## Description

## Problem

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

Port the #1471 design onto `bench-harbor.yml`, reusing the exact same mapping (single source — extract the resolve step into a composite action or shared script if that kills the duplication; otherwise a byte-consistent copy with a cross-reference comment in both files):

1. `provider` choice input (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`) + `provider-config` for custom — same semantics, same validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-looking fields, jq-parse hard-fail).
2. kimi maps to type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384, key env from `secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`.
3. Preflight: selected provider's secret missing → fail in the first minute (today only the zai key is checked at :264).
4. Run identity: workflow/job names + summary carry provider+model (bench.yml pattern: `fa bench · <provider> · <model>`); the free-text `model` input becomes derived-from-provider (keep it as override only for `custom`, or drop it if redundant).
5. REG: default dispatch (no provider input) resolves byte-identical to today's zai glm wiring.
6. `n-concurrent` default is 1 ("z.ai rate-limit safe") — keep for zai; document the kimi-safe value in the input description (kimi coding plan tolerates more; owner picks at dispatch).

## Acceptance

- `bench-harbor.yml` dispatchable with `provider=kimi-for-coding`; smoke run (one task, e.g. the family smoke per docs/bench.md) green on TB 2.1 with kimi.
- actionlint + the workflow-shape tests extended for the new inputs/mapping (mirror of #1475's tests).
- Default-path REG green.

## References

- #1471 (design), PR #1475 (bench.yml implementation to mirror)
- bench-harbor.yml:247-264 (current hardcode)
- kimi wiring precedent: ~/.fah/config.yaml custom providers (apiType kimi, k3-256k)
