def render(splits: dict, expected=None, title=None, ledger=None):
    """Build the summary (lines, problems) — pure, testable.

    title: report heading (family mode, issue #1124); defaults to the
    legacy 4.0 heading. ledger: dict(dataset=, model=, fa_ref=, run_url=)
    — when set, a paste-ready per-version results-ledger row is appended
    with the real cost totals computed below (issue #1124 + #1123).
    """
    lines = [title or "### fa on Terminal-Bench 4.0", ""]
    problems: list[str] = []
    has_jobs = any(rows for rows in splits.values())

    if not has_jobs:
        lines.append("**No harbor jobs found — the run did not complete.**")
        problems.append("no harbor jobs found")
        return lines, problems

    total_resolved = total_rows = 0
    total_in = total_out = total_est = 0
    costs: list[float] = []
    unpriced = 0
    table = [
        "| split | resolved | rate | tokens in/out | est cost |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for split, label in (("cpu", "CPU shards"), ("gpu", "GPU shards")):
        rows = splits[split]
        if not rows:
            table.append(f"| {label} | 0/0 | no trials | — | n/a |")
            continue
        scored = [r for r in rows if not r["exception"]]
        errored = len(rows) - len(scored)
        resolved = sum(1 for r in scored if r["resolved"])
        total_resolved += resolved
        total_rows += len(scored)
        note = f"{errored} errored" if errored else f"{resolved / len(scored):.1%}"
        split_in = sum(r["tokens_in"] for r in scored)
        split_out = sum(r["tokens_out"] for r in scored)
        split_costs = [r["cost"] for r in scored if r["cost"] is not None]
        unpriced += sum(1 for r in scored if r["tokens_in"] and r["cost"] is None)
        costs.extend(split_costs)
        total_in += split_in
        total_out += split_out
        total_est += sum(r["estimated"] for r in scored)

        if total_est:
            lines.append(

def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("jobs_dir", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-trials", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--family", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--model", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--fa-ref", dest="fa_ref", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_url", default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    # Issue #1124: key the report to one dataset family — ignore job dirs
    # from other families so merged artifacts never cross-contaminate.
    job_dirs = [d for d in sorted(args.jobs_dir.glob("*")) if d.is_dir()]
    if args.family:
        job_dirs = [d for d in job_dirs if d.name.startswith(f"fa-{args.family}-")]

    splits: dict[str, list[dict]] = {"cpu": [], "gpu": []}
    for job_dir in job_dirs:
        name = job_dir.name
        if "-gpu-" in name:
            split = "gpu"
        elif "-cpu-" in name:
            split = "cpu"
        else:
            # legacy scheme: docker shards were CPU, modal was the GPU leg
            split = "gpu" if "modal" in name else "cpu"
        splits[split].extend(_trial_rows(job_dir))

    # Lazy: only the family path needs the manifest, and importlib-based
    # test harnesses load this module without the dir on sys.path.
    title = ledger = None
    if args.family:
        import families

        if args.family not in families.FAMILIES:
            # Defense in depth: the workflow resolves the dataset via
            # families.py before dispatch, but a direct summary call must
            # not silently render a mis-keyed report.
            print(
                f"::error::unknown Terminal-Bench family '{args.family}' —"
                f" resolve the dataset id first (families.py resolve);"
                f" known: {', '.join(sorted(families.FAMILIES))}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2

        title = f"### fa on Terminal-Bench {args.family} ({families.FAMILIES[args.family]})"
        ledger = {
            "dataset": families.FAMILIES[args.family],
            "model": args.model or "—",
            "fa_ref": args.fa_ref or "—",
            "run_url": args.run_url or "—",
        }

    lines, problems = render(splits, args.expected_trials, title=title, ledger=ledger)

    if os.environ.get("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"):
        with open(os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"], "a") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    else:
        print("\n".join(lines))

    return 0 if not problems else 1

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

Port the #1471 design onto `bench-harbor.yml`, reusing the exact same mapping (single source — extract the resolve step into a composite action or shared script if that kills the duplication; otherwise a byte-consistent copy with a cross-reference comment in both files):

1. `provider` choice input (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`) + `provider-config` for custom — same semantics, same validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-looking fields, jq-parse hard-fail).
2. kimi maps to type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384, key env from `secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`.
3. Preflight: selected provider's secret missing → fail in the first minute (today only the zai key is checked at :264).
4. Run identity: workflow/job names + summary carry provider+model (bench.yml pattern: `fa bench · <provider> · <model>`); the free-text `model` input becomes derived-from-provider (keep it as override only for `custom`, or drop it if redundant).
5. REG: default dispatch (no provider input) resolves byte-identical to today's zai glm wiring.
6. `n-concurrent` default is 1 ("z.ai rate-limit safe") — keep for zai; document the kimi-safe value in the input description (kimi coding plan tolerates more; owner picks at dispatch).

## Acceptance

- `bench-harbor.yml` dispatchable with `provider=kimi-for-coding`; smoke run (one task, e.g. the family smoke per docs/bench.md) green on TB 2.1 with kimi.
- actionlint + the workflow-shape tests extended for the new inputs/mapping (mirror of #1475's tests).
- Default-path REG green.

- bench-harbor.yml:247-264 (current hardcode)
- kimi wiring precedent: ~/.fah/config.yaml custom providers (apiType kimi, k3-256k)

blocks.text:
name: Bench

# Runs the fa coding agent against terminal-bench on Linux runners
# (issue #125). The `dart build cli` bundle must be a Linux x64 binary to
# match the task container's arch — a macOS host bundle fails with
# "cannot execute binary file", so this cannot run locally on macOS.
#
# Sharded matrix (issue #132): the full terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 dataset
# is 80 tasks at ~11 min each — ~14 h sequential, past even the 6 h job
# cap. Shape: setup (build bundle, resolve task ids into shards) → one
# matrix job per shard → merge job aggregating overall accuracy. Small
# `tasks` inputs degenerate to a single-shard matrix, so the hello-world
# smoke path is unchanged.
#
# Issue #142 (baseline run 34576017658, 26/80 = 32.5%): shards are balanced
# by declared task budget (LPT) instead of contiguous split, tb runs with
# --global-timeout-multiplier 2 (the dataset's declared timeouts — median
# 360s agent / 60s test — assume fast models and warm container networks;
# the baseline lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
# phases still apt-installing their own deps when the cap hit), and the
# bench job patches the downloaded dataset so debian:-based task images
# build again after Debian archived bullseye (expired Release file kills
# `apt-get update` during docker compose build).
#
# Issue #1122: the flat agent cap becomes a per-run ladder — `agent-timeout`
# (base cap seconds) plus optional `progress-extension` (deadline recedes
# while the agent's rendered output grows; idle window 120s, hard ceiling
# 4x base, decisions audited per trial). With both inputs absent the run
# is byte-for-byte today's behavior (dataset declared caps x multiplier;
# REG-1). E3 shard math: with extension on, worst case per task is the
# ceiling (4x agent-timeout) + test budget — the defaults fit the current
# LPT sizing below; raise the ceiling and shrink shards accordingly.
#
# Issue gh-1206 (run 37144207185): the DECLARED test budgets (tb default
# 60s = 120s effective at multiplier 2) classify slow-but-healthy verifier
# phases as test_timeout — jupyter-notebook-server died with the agent's
# pane DONE, the tests having burned their own budget on first-boot
# server startup + in-container dep installs. The test-side analog of the
# #1122 knobs: `test-timeout-floor` (default 120s declared = 240s
# effective) pads every task's max_test_timeout_sec up to the floor in
# the downloaded dataset (patch_test_timeouts.py — the same in-place
# patch mechanism as the Debian apt fix), and shard_tasks.py sizes shards
# on the padded budgets so LPT never under-counts. The cap is a cap, not
# a wait: fast verifier phases are unaffected (a full-dataset worst case
# grows < 10 min/shard); `0` restores the declared budgets.
#
# Issue gh-1407 (runs 37609468473 + 37736364517): the floor alone left
# repeat-offender tasks (jupyter-notebook-server, build-initramfs-qemu)
# test_timeout at the cap in every round — the budget measured runner
# luck, not agent capability. patch_test_timeouts.py additionally applies
# the per-task override table (test_budget_overrides.json, checked in
# next to it: runner-measured test-phase p95 per task, effective budget
# = max(declared, p95 x 1.5) — a slow-suite fix, NOT a global floor
# bump), and shard_tasks.py emits a ::warning:: fairness annotation when
# a planned task's effective test budget is still below its measured
# p95 (fairness_warnings job output), so a structurally-unpassable
# configuration is caught at planning time.
#
# Issue #1392 (bench round 3): retire the artificial timeout class. The
# ×4 ladder ceiling itself was the round-2 killer (play-zork died at 72
# productive minutes), so with progress-extension ON the ladder ceiling
# becomes an absolute one (3600s default, FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC)
# and the outer harness cap pins above THAT — a trial only dies by the
# adapter's verdict (stall / abs ceiling), never tb's flat wait_for. The
# experiment: split 8 shards, run at most `max-concurrent` (default 2) —
# GHA's strategy.max-parallel IS the semaphore. Shards are LPT-packed to
# the job cap minus 15 min headroom; the merge report degrades cancelled
# shards to a `coverage: X/N` note (never red from aggregation), carries
# per-request latency p50/p95 per concurrency level from each trial's
# bench_metrics.json, and names any agent_timeout trial whose session
# gaps never reached the 240s stall threshold (the round-2 contradiction,
# AC8).
# gh-1471 (run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks when the z.ai quota died
# mid-run): the provider stops being a hardcode — every dispatch picks
# zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to today) or kimi-for-coding
# k3-256k via a dedicated FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY (never the review factory's
# KIMI_REVIEW_KEY — one quota must not serve both), or `custom`: a
# provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step (https-only baseUrl,
# no key-like fields — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata) whose
# key comes only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM. A
# setup-job resolve step maps the choice to the full provider triple and
# preflights the selected secret BEFORE any shard starts (presence only,
# never a value); the shard job names the provider+model (job `name:`
# CAN read needs outputs — unlike env), and the summary report tags it
# (BENCH_RUN_LABEL) so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/cost
# views.
run-name: fa bench · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider…

name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issu…

blocks.text:
name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Resolve the dispatch input (family label, bare version, or full
      # Harbor id) to the canonical dataset id; unknown or version-less
      # specs fail fast here, before any download.
      - name: Resolve Terminal-Bench family
        id: family
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
        run: python bench/harbor_fa/families.py resolve "$DATASET"

      # Cost guard (issue #1124 E3): full runs of the intermediate
      # families are hours of GPU + LLM spend — require explicit
      # confirmation. Smoke runs (non-empty tasks) and 4.0 (the
      # historical default, AC4) are unaffected.
      - name: Confirm full intermediate-family run
        if: steps.family.outputs.family != '4.0' && inputs.confirm-full-run != true
        env:
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
        run: |
          # split_tasks.py strips each comma-glob before use, so " ", ",",
          # " , " all normalize to zero globs = a FULL dataset run. Judge
          # emptiness on that same normalization, not the raw input.
          if [ -z "$(printf %s "$TASKS" | tr -d '[:space:],')" ]; then
            echo "::error::Full run of Terminal-Bench ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }} (${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}, ~${{ steps.family.outputs.tasks }} tasks x $ATTEMPTS attempts) requires confirm-full-run: true. Smoke first: tasks=${{ steps.family.outputs.smoke }}, attempts=1 (docs/bench.md)."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) and bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py
      # plumbing the bench dirs don't have.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
         …

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pins the knob/timeout shell logic of the bench.yml shard step (gh-1209).

The `run:` block decides, from two workflow_dispatch inputs, whether the
outer tb harness cap must sit above the progress ladder's ceiling and which
env vars reach fa_agent.py. This suite executes that exact block against a
`tb` stub and pins one behavior per input combination:

- REG-1 (issue #1122): both inputs absent → byte-for-byte stock delegation —
  no FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC, no FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION, no --global-agent-
  timeout-sec.
- gh-1209: any active ladder (explicit agent-timeout, or progress-extension
  on with its 360s default base) pins the harness cap at 4x base + 180s so
  the ladder decides, never the flat harness wait_for.
- gh-1209 review: `agent-timeout=0` is rejected at step start — it used to
  pass validation, export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC=0, and raise ValueError
  inside EVERY trial's perform_task hours into the shard.
- Invalid inputs (non-digit timeout, non-boolean extension) fail fast.

Issue #1406: the fa launch path must carry the ConnTrace env into the
tmux pane itself (string-level asserts on the generated TerminalCommand
— the exact bytes tb types into the pane), and a trial whose
bench_metrics.json folded zero requests despite real model usage must
fire a LOUD workflow warning, never ship an empty shell silently.

gh-1471: the setup-job provider resolve step maps the dispatch choice
(zai-glm-5.3-flash default / kimi-for-coding / custom) to the full
provider triple and preflights the selected secret BEFORE any shard
starts — each choice pins (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar), an
unmapped value fails hard, a missing secret fails fast naming the
secret, and a key value never reaches the log. The custom path (D1 /
AC 2a) validates the provider-config JSON (parseable object, non-empty
https:// baseUrl + model, no key-like fields case-insensitively at any
depth, plus the Dart preconfig contract mirror: closed key whitelist,
capability integer+floor pair, type/input/thinkingLevel shapes) and
injects the fixed apiKeyEnvVar FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM — the key comes only
from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY. REG-1: the default's provider_config is
byte-identical to the pre-gh-1471 3-field zai JSON.

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
"""
import importlib.util
import collections
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import types
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stderr
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
_BENCH_YML = _REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "bench.yml"
sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT / "bench"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

import bench_metrics  # noqa: E402


def _shard_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the tb shard step from bench.yml.

    Text-slicing, not PyYAML: the block is a literal scalar and the suite
    must run anywhere python3 runs (the bench shards have no PyYAML). The
    block is identified by its `tb run -d` body, so unrelated `run:` blocks
    never match.
    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)
        while body and not body[-1].strip():
            body.pop()
        block = "\n".join(body)
        if "tb run -d" in block:
            start = True
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError("tb shard step's run: | block not found in bench.yml")
    # Only expression the block may interpolate; anything else means the
    # workflow grew a new one and this harness needs the mapping extended.
    block = re.sub(r"\$\{\{\s*matrix\.i\s*\}\}", "0", block)
    leftover = re.findall(r"\$\{\{[^}]*\}\}", block)
    assert not leftover, f"unmapped GitHub expression(s) in run block: {leftover}"
    return block


def _resolve_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the gh-1471 provider resolve step.

    Same text-slicing contract as [_shard_run_block]: the block is
    identified by its body (the provider_config printf), so unrelated
    `run:` blocks never match. The block is env-driven (inputs/secrets
    arrive via the step env), so no GitHub expression may appear inside.
    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)
        while body and not body[-1].strip():
            body.pop()
        block = "\n".join(body)
        if "provider_config=$(printf" in block:
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError("provider resolve step's run: | block not found in bench.yml")
    leftover = re.findall(r"\$\{\{[^}]*\}\}", block)
    assert not leftover, f"unmapped GitHub expression(s) in resolve block: {leftover}"
    return block


# The resolve block runs with GITHUB_OUTPUT pointed at a temp file (the
# test reads the step outputs from it) and all three bench secrets in env
# (gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: the custom path preflights FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY).
def _run_resolve(
    provider="",
    zai_key="zai-test-key",
    kimi_key="kimi-test-key",
    custom_key="custom-test-key",
    provider_config="",
):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update(
        {
            "PROVIDER": provider,
            "BENCH_MODEL": "glm-5.3-flash",
            "PROVIDER_CONFIG": provider_config,
            "FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY": zai_key,
            "FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY": kimi_key,
            "FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY": custom_key,
        }
    )
    tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
    output = Path(tmp.name) / "github_output"
    env["GITHUB_OUTPUT"] = str(output)
    driver = Path(tmp.name) / "resolve_step.sh"
    driver.write_text("#!/usr/bin/env bash\n" + _resolve_run_block() + "\n")
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["bash", str(driver)],
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=30,
    )
    proc._tmp = tmp  # caller cleans up after reading the outputs
    proc.github_output = output
    return proc


def _resolve_outputs(proc) -> dict:
    if not proc.github_output.exists():
        return {}
    result = {}
    for line in proc.github_output.read_text().splitlines():
        if "=" in line:
            key, _, value = line.partition("=")
            result[key] = value
    proc._tmp.cleanup()
    return result


# The tb stub records the exact argv the block computed plus the two env
# vars fa_agent.py's TimeoutKnobs reads, then exits 0 — the real tb never
# runs in tests.
_TB_STUB = r"""
tb() {
  echo "TB_BEGIN"

  echo "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC=${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC-__unset__}"
}
"""

_DRIVER = "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n" + _TB_STUB + "\n" + _shard_run_block() + "\n"

class _FakeFoldContainer:
    """exec_run surface for the fold: session JSONL + the env-proof cat.

    Returns a namedtuple like docker's ExecResult — fa_agent consumes
    exec_run both as a tuple (fold) and by attribute (pane taps).
    """

    _Exec = collections.namedtuple("_Exec", ["exit_code", "output"])

    def __init__(self, session_jsonl, env_proof):
        self._session_jsonl = session_jsonl
        self._env_proof = env_proof

    def exec_run(self, cmd, **kwargs):
        joined = " ".join(cmd)
        if "find" in joined and "-exec cat" in joined:
            return self._Exec(0, self._session_jsonl.encode())
        if "cat /tmp/fa-conn-env.txt" in joined:
            return self._Exec(0, self._env_proof)
        return self._Exec(0, b"")

    def get_archive(self, path):
        return ([b""], "unused.tar")


class _FakeFoldSession:
    """Minimal TmuxSession surface: just the container the fold touches."""

    def __init__(self, container):
        self.container = container


class FoldWiringTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """The usage fold is the common terminal path of BOTH adapter modes
    (stock and deadline) — the env-proof fold and the loud-empty guard
    must hang off it, so every bench trial gets them."""

    maxDiff = None

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.fa_agent = _load_fa_agent_1406()

    def test_fold_writes_env_proof_and_fires_the_guard(self):
        tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(tmpdir.cleanup)
        logging_dir = Path(tmpdir.name) / "t0"
        logging_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
        (logging_dir / "bench_metrics.json").write_text(
            json.dumps({"trial": "t0", "requests": []})
        )
        session = _FakeFoldSession(
            _FakeFoldContainer(
                session_jsonl=(
                    '{"timestamp":"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z","message":{"role":"assistant",'
                    '"model":"m","usage":{"input":10,"output":5}}}\n'
                ),
                env_proof=(
                    b"FA_CONN_DEBUG=1\n"
                    b"FA_CONN_TRACE_FILE=/tmp/fa-conn-trace.jsonl\n"
                ),
            )
        )
        result = self.fa_agent.AgentResult(total_input_tokens=0, total_output_tokens=0)
        err = StringIO()
        with redirect_stderr(err):
            self.fa_agent.FaAgent._fold_session_usage(session, result, logging_dir)
        # Usage folded from the session records...
        self.assertEqual(result.total_input_tokens, 10)
        self.assertEqual(result.total_output_tokens, 5)
        # ...the launch-time env proof landed in agent-logs (AC1)...
        proof = (logging_dir / "fa-conn-env.txt").read_text()
        self.assertIn("FA_CONN_DEBUG=1", proof)
        # ...and the dark-ConnTrace trial fired the loud-empty guard (AC2).
        self.assertIn("BENCH METRICS GUARD", err.getvalue())
        guard = json.loads((logging_dir / "conn-guard.json").read_text())
        self.assertFalse(guard["ok"])
        self.assertEqual(guard["usage_tokens"], 15)

    def test_env_proof_fold_is_fail_soft(self):
        # A broken/wedged container must never fail the trial over a
        # proof artifact (same contract as every other fold step).
        class _BoomContainer:
            def exec_run(self, cmd, **kwargs):
                raise RuntimeError("container gone")

        err = StringIO()
        with redirect_stderr(err):
            self.fa_agent.FaAgent._write_conn_env_proof(
                _FakeFoldSession(_BoomContainer()), Path(tmp_dir := tempfile.mkdtemp())
            )
        self.assertIn("conn env proof not written", err.getvalue())
        self.assertFalse((Path(tmp_dir) / "fa-conn-env.txt").exists())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def name() -> str:
        return "fa"

    def version(self) -> str | None:
        return self._version or _VERSION

    def get_version_command(self) -> str | None:
        return "fa --version"

    @property
    def _bundle_tarball(self) -> Path:
        return Path(os.environ.get("FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL", "fa-bundle.tar.gz"))

    @property
    def _provider_env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        # Everything crosses base64-encoded: exec env values pass through
        # shell export lines, and base64 keeps arbitrary JSON/keys safe.
        # Secrets live env-only, never echoed (only masked in CI logs).
        env = {
            "FA_PROVIDER_TYPE": os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_TYPE", "anthropic"),
            "FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64": _b64(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]),
        }
        # Issue #1408 AC1: fa's bash-job logs (.fah/bash_jobs/) used to land
        # INSIDE the task workspace, capturing raw secret values from the
        # agent's own greps; the graded diff (test_no_other_files_changed)
        # then failed on the agent sanitizing the harness's own logs.
        # Relocate them outside the workspace — /tmp is the in-container
        # twin of the runner's $RUNNER_TEMP (same dir the tb adapter uses).
        env["FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR"] = _CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR
        key_var = json.loads(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]).get("apiKeyEnvVar")
        if key_var and os.environ.get(key_var):
            env[f"{key_var}_BASE64"] = _b64(os.environ[key_var])
        return env

    async def install(self, environment: BaseEnvironment) -> None:
        tarball = self._bundle_tarball
        if not tarball.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"fa bundle tarball not found: {tarball} — build it with "
                f"`dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart`"
            )
        remote_tarball = "/tmp/fa-bundle.tar.gz"
        await environment.upload_file(tarball, remote_tarball)
        await self.exec_as_root(
            environment,
            command=(
                f"mkdir -p /opt/fa && tar -xzf {remote_tarball} -C /opt/fa && "
                "chmod +x /opt/fa/bin/fah && ln -sf /opt/fa/bin/fah /usr/local/bin/fa"
            ),
        )
        # Task images ship without CA roots — Dart TLS then dies with
        # CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED on the provider handshake (live smoke,
        # run 34741686224). Best-effort bootstrap across common distros;
        # a no-op where the store already exists.
        await self.exec_as_root(
            environment,
            command=(
                "if [ ! -e /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt ]; then "
                "if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then "
                "apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq ca-certificates; "
                "elif command -v apk >/dev/null; then apk add --no-cache ca-certificates; "

Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `model` — default `glm-5.3-flash` (recorded with the run; the provider
  preconfig below is what fa actually connects with).
- `attempts` — harbor `-k` trials per task, default `5` (leaderboard protocol).
- `n-concurrent` — default `1` (z.ai rate limits; raise with care).
- `shards` — CPU docker shards, default `16` (~4 tasks/shard keeps each
  job inside the job window; raise to ~22 for the 89-task 2.x sets).
  Shards run up to 5 in parallel on the default ubuntu runners.
- `cpu-env` — Harbor env for the CPU shards, default `docker` (issue
  #1316: local docker, no Modal/cloud dependency); `modal` for the
  self-hosted path.
- `cpu-runner` — runner label for the docker shards, default
  `ubuntu-latest` (GH runners ship docker); `self-hosted` for the modal
  path.

Smoke first, per family: dispatch with `tasks: <smoke task from the
table>, attempts: 1` (e.g. `dataset: 2.1, tasks: fix-git, attempts: 1`).
Once green, dispatch the full run (`tasks:` empty,
`confirm-full-run: true` for 2.0/2.1/3.0).

Comparability discipline (issue #1124): a cross-version run set uses the
**same model and the same fa bundle** (commit) for every version, and
each ledger row names both.

Tool error (bash): # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
---

def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("jobs_dir", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-trials", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--family", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--model", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--fa-ref", dest="fa_ref", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_url", default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    # Issue #1124: key the report to one dataset family — ignore job dirs
    # from other families so merged artifacts never cross-contaminate.
    job_dirs = [d for d in sorted(args.jobs_dir.glob("*")) if d.is_dir()]
    if args.family:
        job_dirs = [d for d in job_dirs if d.name.startswith(f"fa-{args.family}-")]

    splits: dict[str, list[dict]] = {"cpu": [], "gpu": []}
    for job_dir in job_dirs:
        name = job_dir.name
        if "-gpu-" in name:
            split = "gpu"
        elif "-cpu-" in name:
            split = "cpu"
        else:
            # legacy scheme: docker shards were CPU, modal was the GPU leg
            split = "gpu" if "modal" in name else "cpu"
        splits[split].extend(_trial_rows(job_dir))

    # Lazy: only the family path needs the manifest, and importlib-based
    # test harnesses load this module without the dir on sys.path.
    title = ledger = None
    if args.family:
        import families

        if args.family not in families.FAMILIES:
            # Defense in depth: the workflow resolves the dataset via
            # families.py before dispatch, but a direct summary call must
            # not silently render a mis-keyed report.
            print(
                f"::error::unknown Terminal-Bench family '{args.family}' —"
                f" resolve the dataset id first (families.py resolve);"
                f" known: {', '.join(sorted(families.FAMILIES))}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2

        title = f"### fa on Terminal-Bench {args.family} ({families.FAMILIES[args.family]})"
        ledger = {
            "dataset": families.FAMILIES[args.family],
            "model": args.model or "—",
            "fa_ref": args.fa_ref or "—",
            "run_url": args.run_url or "—",
        }

    lines, problems = render(splits, args.expected_trials, title=title, ledger=ledger)

    if os.environ.get("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"):
        with open(os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"], "a") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    else:
        print("\n".join(lines))

    return 0 if not problems else 1

blocks.text:
# gh-1503: [ENH] bench-harbor.yml: port gh-1471 provider selection (kimi-for-coding + custom) — TB2.x bench path is zai-only

## Description

## Problem

gh-1471 added provider selection to `bench.yml` (TB1 core, PR #1475 — merged): dispatch input `provider` (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`), dedicated secrets (`FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`), missing-key preflight, run-identity naming.

`bench-harbor.yml` (Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 via Harbor) is still **hardcoded to z.ai**: `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai`, `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` glm-5.3-flash (:247-248), preflight only for `FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY` (:264), model recorded via the free-text `model` input. With the z.ai budget at zero, the entire TB2+ bench path is unusable.

## Requirement

Port the #1471 design onto `bench-harbor.yml`, reusing the exact same mapping (single source — extract the resolve step into a composite action or shared script if that kills the duplication; otherwise a byte-consistent copy with a cross-reference comment in both files):

1. `provider` choice input (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding` / `custom`) + `provider-config` for custom — same semantics, same validation (https-only baseUrl, no key-looking fields, jq-parse hard-fail).
2. kimi maps to type `kimi`, baseUrl `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, model `k3-256k`, contextWindow 200000, maxTokens 16384, key env from `secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`.
3. Preflight: selected provider's secret missing → fail in the first minute (today only the zai key is checked at :264).
4. Run identity: workflow/job names + summary carry provider+model (bench.yml pattern: `fa bench · <provider> · <model>`); the free-text `model` input becomes derived-from-provider (keep it as override only for `custom`, or drop it if redundant).
5. REG: default dispatch (no provider input) resolves byte-identical to today's zai glm wiring.
6. `n-concurrent` default is 1 ("z.ai rate-limit safe") — keep for zai; document the kimi-safe value in the input description (kimi coding plan tolerates more; owner picks at dispatch).

## Acceptance

- `bench-harbor.yml` dispatchable with `provider=kimi-for-coding`; smoke run (one task, e.g. the family smoke per docs/bench.md) green on TB 2.1 with kimi.
- actionlint + the workflow-shape tests extended for the new inputs/mapping (mirror of #1475's tests).
- Default-path REG green.

## References

- #1471 (design), PR #1475 (bench.yml implementation to mirror)
- bench-harbor.yml:247-264 (current hardcode)
- kimi wiring precedent: ~/.fah/config.yaml custom providers (apiType kimi, k3-256k)

blocks.text:
name: Bench

# Runs the fa coding agent against terminal-bench on Linux runners
# (issue #125). The `dart build cli` bundle must be a Linux x64 binary to
# match the task container's arch — a macOS host bundle fails with
# "cannot execute binary file", so this cannot run locally on macOS.
#
# Sharded matrix (issue #132): the full terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 dataset
# is 80 tasks at ~11 min each — ~14 h sequential, past even the 6 h job
# cap. Shape: setup (build bundle, resolve task ids into shards) → one
# matrix job per shard → merge job aggregating overall accuracy. Small
# `tasks` inputs degenerate to a single-shard matrix, so the hello-world
# smoke path is unchanged.
#
# Issue #142 (baseline run 34576017658, 26/80 = 32.5%): shards are balanced
# by declared task budget (LPT) instead of contiguous split, tb runs with
# --global-timeout-multiplier 2 (the dataset's declared timeouts — median
# 360s agent / 60s test — assume fast models and warm container networks;
# the baseline lost trials to agents killed mid-progress and to test
# phases still apt-installing their own deps when the cap hit), and the
# bench job patches the downloaded dataset so debian:-based task images
# build again after Debian archived bullseye (expired Release file kills
# `apt-get update` during docker compose build).
#
# Issue #1122: the flat agent cap becomes a per-run ladder — `agent-timeout`
# (base cap seconds) plus optional `progress-extension` (deadline recedes
# while the agent's rendered output grows; idle window 120s, hard ceiling
# 4x base, decisions audited per trial). With both inputs absent the run
# is byte-for-byte today's behavior (dataset declared caps x multiplier;
# REG-1). E3 shard math: with extension on, worst case per task is the
# ceiling (4x agent-timeout) + test budget — the defaults fit the current
# LPT sizing below; raise the ceiling and shrink shards accordingly.
#
# Issue gh-1206 (run 37144207185): the DECLARED test budgets (tb default
# 60s = 120s effective at multiplier 2) classify slow-but-healthy verifier
# phases as test_timeout — jupyter-notebook-server died with the agent's
# pane DONE, the tests having burned their own budget on first-boot
# server startup + in-container dep installs. The test-side analog of the
# #1122 knobs: `test-timeout-floor` (default 120s declared = 240s
# effective) pads every task's max_test_timeout_sec up to the floor in
# the downloaded dataset (patch_test_timeouts.py — the same in-place
# patch mechanism as the Debian apt fix), and shard_tasks.py sizes shards
# on the padded budgets so LPT never under-counts. The cap is a cap, not
# a wait: fast verifier phases are unaffected (a full-dataset worst case
# grows < 10 min/shard); `0` restores the declared budgets.
#
# Issue gh-1407 (runs 37609468473 + 37736364517): the floor alone left
# repeat-offender tasks (jupyter-notebook-server, build-initramfs-qemu)
# test_timeout at the cap in every round — the budget measured runner
# luck, not agent capability. patch_test_timeouts.py additionally applies
# the per-task override table (test_budget_overrides.json, checked in
# next to it: runner-measured test-phase p95 per task, effective budget
# = max(declared, p95 x 1.5) — a slow-suite fix, NOT a global floor
# bump), and shard_tasks.py emits a ::warning:: fairness annotation when
# a planned task's effective test budget is still below its measured
# p95 (fairness_warnings job output), so a structurally-unpassable
# configuration is caught at planning time.
#
# Issue #1392 (bench round 3): retire the artificial timeout class. The
# ×4 ladder ceiling itself was the round-2 killer (play-zork died at 72
# productive minutes), so with progress-extension ON the ladder ceiling
# becomes an absolute one (3600s default, FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC)
# and the outer harness cap pins above THAT — a trial only dies by the
# adapter's verdict (stall / abs ceiling), never tb's flat wait_for. The
# experiment: split 8 shards, run at most `max-concurrent` (default 2) —
# GHA's strategy.max-parallel IS the semaphore. Shards are LPT-packed to
# the job cap minus 15 min headroom; the merge report degrades cancelled
# shards to a `coverage: X/N` note (never red from aggregation), carries
# per-request latency p50/p95 per concurrency level from each trial's
# bench_metrics.json, and names any agent_timeout trial whose session
# gaps never reached the 240s stall threshold (the round-2 contradiction,
# AC8).
# gh-1471 (run 37953576205 lost 14/78 tasks when the z.ai quota died
# mid-run): the provider stops being a hardcode — every dispatch picks
# zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to today) or kimi-for-coding
# k3-256k via a dedicated FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY (never the review factory's
# KIMI_REVIEW_KEY — one quota must not serve both), or `custom`: a
# provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step (https-only baseUrl,
# no key-like fields — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata) whose
# key comes only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM. A
# setup-job resolve step maps the choice to the full provider triple and
# preflights the selected secret BEFORE any shard starts (presence only,
# never a value); the shard job names the provider+model (job `name:`
# CAN read needs outputs — unlike env), and the summary report tags it
# (BENCH_RUN_LABEL) so glm and kimi runs never blend in the history/cost
# views.
run-name: fa bench · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider…

blocks.text:
name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pins the knob/timeout shell logic of the bench.yml shard step (gh-1209).

The `run:` block decides, from two workflow_dispatch inputs, whether the
outer tb harness cap must sit above the progress ladder's ceiling and which
env vars reach fa_agent.py. This suite executes that exact block against a
`tb` stub and pins one behavior per input combination:

- REG-1 (issue #1122): both inputs absent → byte-for-byte stock delegation —
  no FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC, no FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION, no --global-agent-
  timeout-sec.
- gh-1209: any active ladder (explicit agent-timeout, or progress-extension
  on with its 360s default base) pins the harness cap at 4x base + 180s so
  the ladder decides, never the flat harness wait_for.
- gh-1209 review: `agent-timeout=0` is rejected at step start — it used to
  pass validation, export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC=0, and raise ValueError
  inside EVERY trial's perform_task hours into the shard.
- Invalid inputs (non-digit timeout, non-boolean extension) fail fast.

Issue #1406: the fa launch path must carry the ConnTrace env into the
tmux pane itself (string-level asserts on the generated TerminalCommand
— the exact bytes tb types into the pane), and a trial whose
bench_metrics.json folded zero requests despite real model usage must
fire a LOUD workflow warning, never ship an empty shell silently.

gh-1471: the setup-job provider resolve step maps the dispatch choice
(zai-glm-5.3-flash default / kimi-for-coding / custom) to the full
provider triple and preflights the selected secret BEFORE any shard
starts — each choice pins (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar), an
unmapped value fails hard, a missing secret fails fast naming the
secret, and a key value never reaches the log. The custom path (D1 /
AC 2a) validates the provider-config JSON (parseable object, non-empty
https:// baseUrl + model, no key-like fields case-insensitively at any
depth, plus the Dart preconfig contract mirror: closed key whitelist,
capability integer+floor pair, type/input/thinkingLevel shapes) and
injects the fixed apiKeyEnvVar FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM — the key comes only
from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY. REG-1: the default's provider_config is
byte-identical to the pre-gh-1471 3-field zai JSON.

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
"""
import importlib.util
import collections
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import types
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stderr
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
_BENCH_YML = _REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "bench.yml"
sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT / "bench"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

import bench_metrics  # noqa: E402


def _shard_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the tb shard step from bench.yml.

    Text-slicing, not PyYAML: the block is a literal scalar and the suite
    must run anywhere python3 runs (the bench shards have no PyYAML). The
    block is identified by its `tb run -d` body, so unrelated `run:` blocks
    never match.
    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)
        while body and not body[-1].strip():
            body.pop()
        block = "\n".join(body)
        if "tb run -d" in block:
            start = True
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError("tb shard step's run: | block not found in bench.yml")
    # Only expression the block may interpolate; anything else means the
    # workflow grew a new one and this harness needs the mapping extended.
    block = re.sub(r"\$\{\{\s*matrix\.i\s*\}\}", "0", block)
    leftover = re.findall(r"\$\{\{[^}]*\}\}", block)
    assert not leftover, f"unmapped GitHub expression(s) in run block: {leftover}"
    return block


def _resolve_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the gh-1471 provider resolve step.

    Same text-slicing contract as [_shard_run_block]: the block is
    identified by its body (the provider_config printf), so unrelated
    `run:` blocks never match. The block is env-driven (inputs/secrets
    arrive via the step env), so no GitHub expression may appear inside.
    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)
        while body and not body[-1].strip():
            body.pop()
        block = "\n".join(body)
        if "provider_config=$(printf" in block:
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError("provider resolve step's run: | block not found in bench.yml")
    leftover = re.findall(r"\$\{\{[^}]*\}\}", block)
    assert not leftover, f"unmapped GitHub expression(s) in resolve block: {leftover}"
    return block


# The resolve block runs with GITHUB_OUTPUT pointed at a temp file (the
# test reads the step outputs from it) and all three bench secrets in env
# (gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: the custom path preflights FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY).
def _run_resolve(
    provider="",
    zai_key="zai-test-key",
    kimi_key="kimi-test-key",
    custom_key="custom-test-key",
    provider_config="",
):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update(
        {
            "PROVIDER": provider,
            "BENCH_MODEL": "glm-5.3-flash",
            "PROVIDER_CONFIG": provider_config,
            "FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY": zai_key,
            "FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY": kimi_key,
            "FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY": custom_key,
        }
    )
    tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
    output = Path(tmp.name) / "github_output"
    env["GITHUB_OUTPUT"] = str(output)
    driver = Path(tmp.name) / "resolve_step.sh"
    driver.write_text("#!/usr/bin/env bash\n" + _resolve_run_block() + "\n")
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["bash", str(driver)],
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=30,
    )
    proc._tmp = tmp  # caller cleans up after reading the outputs
    proc.github_output = output
    return proc


def _resolve_outputs(proc) -> dict:
    if not proc.github_output.exists():
        return {}
    result = {}
    for line in proc.github_output.read_text().splitlines():
        if "=" in line:
            key, _, value = line.partition("=")
            result[key] = value
    proc._tmp.cleanup()
    return result


# The tb stub records the exact argv the block computed plus the two env
# vars fa_agent.py's TimeoutKnobs reads, then exits 0 — the real tb never
# runs in tests.
_TB_STUB = r"""
tb() {
  echo "TB_BEGIN"

}
"""

_DRIVER = "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n" + _TB_STUB + "\n" + _shard_run_block() + "\n"

class _FakeFoldContainer:
    """exec_run surface for the fold: session JSONL + the env-proof cat.

    Returns a namedtuple like docker's ExecResult — fa_agent consumes
    exec_run both as a tuple (fold) and by attribute (pane taps).
    """

    _Exec = collections.namedtuple("_Exec", ["exit_code", "output"])

    def __init__(self, session_jsonl, env_proof):
        self._session_jsonl = session_jsonl
        self._env_proof = env_proof

    def exec_run(self, cmd, **kwargs):
        joined = " ".join(cmd)
        if "find" in joined and "-exec cat" in joined:
            return self._Exec(0, self._session_jsonl.encode())
        if "cat /tmp/fa-conn-env.txt" in joined:
            return self._Exec(0, self._env_proof)
        return self._Exec(0, b"")

    def get_archive(self, path):
        return ([b""], "unused.tar")


class _FakeFoldSession:
    """Minimal TmuxSession surface: just the container the fold touches."""

    def __init__(self, container):
        self.container = container


class FoldWiringTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """The usage fold is the common terminal path of BOTH adapter modes
    (stock and deadline) — the env-proof fold and the loud-empty guard
    must hang off it, so every bench trial gets them."""

    maxDiff = None

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.fa_agent = _load_fa_agent_1406()

    def test_fold_writes_env_proof_and_fires_the_guard(self):
        tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(tmpdir.cleanup)
        logging_dir = Path(tmpdir.name) / "t0"
        logging_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
        (logging_dir / "bench_metrics.json").write_text(
            json.dumps({"trial": "t0", "requests": []})
        )
        session = _FakeFoldSession(
            _FakeFoldContainer(
                session_jsonl=(
                    '{"timestamp":"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z","message":{"role":"assistant",'
                    '"model":"m","usage":{"input":10,"output":5}}}\n'
                ),
                env_proof=(
                    b"FA_CONN_DEBUG=1\n"
                    b"FA_CONN_TRACE_FILE=/tmp/fa-conn-trace.jsonl\n"
                ),
            )
        )
        result = self.fa_agent.AgentResult(total_input_tokens=0, total_output_tokens=0)
        err = StringIO()
        with redirect_stderr(err):
            self.fa_agent.FaAgent._fold_session_usage(session, result, logging_dir)
        # Usage folded from the session records...
        self.assertEqual(result.total_input_tokens, 10)
        self.assertEqual(result.total_output_tokens, 5)
        # ...the launch-time env proof landed in agent-logs (AC1)...
        proof = (logging_dir / "fa-conn-env.txt").read_text()
        self.assertIn("FA_CONN_DEBUG=1", proof)
        # ...and the dark-ConnTrace trial fired the loud-empty guard (AC2).
        self.assertIn("BENCH METRICS GUARD", err.getvalue())
        guard = json.loads((logging_dir / "conn-guard.json").read_text())
        self.assertFalse(guard["ok"])
        self.assertEqual(guard["usage_tokens"], 15)

    def test_env_proof_fold_is_fail_soft(self):
        # A broken/wedged container must never fail the trial over a
        # proof artifact (same contract as every other fold step).
        class _BoomContainer:
            def exec_run(self, cmd, **kwargs):
                raise RuntimeError("container gone")

        err = StringIO()
        with redirect_stderr(err):
            self.fa_agent.FaAgent._write_conn_env_proof(
                _FakeFoldSession(_BoomContainer()), Path(tmp_dir := tempfile.mkdtemp())
            )
        self.assertIn("conn env proof not written", err.getvalue())
        self.assertFalse((Path(tmp_dir) / "fa-conn-env.txt").exists())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def name() -> str:
        return "fa"

    def version(self) -> str | None:
        return self._version or _VERSION

    def get_version_command(self) -> str | None:
        return "fa --version"

    @property
    def _bundle_tarball(self) -> Path:
        return Path(os.environ.get("FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL", "fa-bundle.tar.gz"))

    @property
    def _provider_env(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        # Everything crosses base64-encoded: exec env values pass through
        # shell export lines, and base64 keeps arbitrary JSON/keys safe.
        # Secrets live env-only, never echoed (only masked in CI logs).
        env = {
            "FA_PROVIDER_TYPE": os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_TYPE", "anthropic"),
            "FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG_BASE64": _b64(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]),
        }
        # Issue #1408 AC1: fa's bash-job logs (.fah/bash_jobs/) used to land
        # INSIDE the task workspace, capturing raw secret values from the
        # agent's own greps; the graded diff (test_no_other_files_changed)
        # then failed on the agent sanitizing the harness's own logs.
        # Relocate them outside the workspace — /tmp is the in-container
        # twin of the runner's $RUNNER_TEMP (same dir the tb adapter uses).
        env["FAH_JOB_LOG_DIR"] = _CONTAINER_JOB_LOG_DIR
        key_var = json.loads(os.environ["FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG"]).get("apiKeyEnvVar")
        if key_var and os.environ.get(key_var):
            env[f"{key_var}_BASE64"] = _b64(os.environ[key_var])
        return env

    async def install(self, environment: BaseEnvironment) -> None:
        tarball = self._bundle_tarball
        if not tarball.is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"fa bundle tarball not found: {tarball} — build it with "
                f"`dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart`"
            )
        remote_tarball = "/tmp/fa-bundle.tar.gz"
        await environment.upload_file(tarball, remote_tarball)
        await self.exec_as_root(
            environment,
            command=(
                f"mkdir -p /opt/fa && tar -xzf {remote_tarball} -C /opt/fa && "
                "chmod +x /opt/fa/bin/fah && ln -sf /opt/fa/bin/fah /usr/local/bin/fa"
            ),
        )
        # Task images ship without CA roots — Dart TLS then dies with
        # CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED on the provider handshake (live smoke,
        # run 34741686224). Best-effort bootstrap across common distros;
        # a no-op where the store already exists.
        await self.exec_as_root(
            environment,
            command=(
                "if [ ! -e /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt ]; then "
                "if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then "
                "apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq ca-certificates; "
                "elif command -v apk >/dev/null; then apk add --no-cache ca-certificates; "

Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `model` — default `glm-5.3-flash` (recorded with the run; the provider
  preconfig below is what fa actually connects with).
- `attempts` — harbor `-k` trials per task, default `5` (leaderboard protocol).
- `n-concurrent` — default `1` (z.ai rate limits; raise with care).
- `shards` — CPU docker shards, default `16` (~4 tasks/shard keeps each
  job inside the job window; raise to ~22 for the 89-task 2.x sets).
  Shards run up to 5 in parallel on the default ubuntu runners.
- `cpu-env` — Harbor env for the CPU shards, default `docker` (issue
  #1316: local docker, no Modal/cloud dependency); `modal` for the
  self-hosted path.
- `cpu-runner` — runner label for the docker shards, default
  `ubuntu-latest` (GH runners ship docker); `self-hosted` for the modal
  path.

Smoke first, per family: dispatch with `tasks: <smoke task from the
table>, attempts: 1` (e.g. `dataset: 2.1, tasks: fix-git, attempts: 1`).
Once green, dispatch the full run (`tasks:` empty,
`confirm-full-run: true` for 2.0/2.1/3.0).

Tool error (bash): # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
---
